summary: The root أجج (Ajj) primarily describes the act of kindling or setting something ablaze, causing it to burn fiercely.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: أَجَّتِ النَّارُ, (S, A, Msb,) aor. اَجُجَ (S, Msb) and اَجِجَ, (M, TA,) [the former contr. to analogy, and the latter agreeable therewith, in the case of an intrans. verb of this class,] inf. n. أَجِيحٌ, (S, A, Msb, K,) The fire burned, burned up, burned brightly, or fiercely, (Msb,) blazed, or flamed, or blazed or flamed fiercely; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also (S, A, K) and [written with the disjunctive alif اِيتَجَّت ]: (S, K:) or made a sound by its blazing or flaming. (ISd, TA.) أَجَّ, aor.

أجّج النَّارَ, (S, A, K,) inf. n. تَأْجِيحٌ, (K,) He made the fire to [ burn, burn up, burn brightly or fiercely, (see 1,)] blaze, or flame, or blaze or flame fiercely. (S, A, K.) [Hence,] أجّج بَيْنَهُمْ شَرَّا (assumed tropical:) He kindled evil, or mischief, among them. (TA.)
تَاَجَّجَ see 1. Hence تإجّج also signifies It gave light; shone; or shone brightly. (TA, from a trad.) See also 8, where a contracted form of this verb is mentioned.
إِاْتَجَجَ see 1. [Hence,] ائتجّ النَّهَارُ [written with the disjunctive alif اِيْتَجَّ ] The day was, or became, intensely hot, or fiercely burning; (S, K;) as also and تأجّج. (K.)

أَجَّةٌ Intenseness of heat, and its fierce burning; (S, K;) as also [inf. n. of 1], and, and [inf. N. of 8]: pl. إِجَاجٌ. (S.) You say, جَآتْ أَجَّةٌ الصَّيْفِ The intense heat, or fierce burning, of summer came. (TA.) The sound of fire; as also. (ISd, TA.) (tropical:) The sound, or noise, and commotion, of an ostrich running, and of people walking or passing along. (A.) You say, أَجَّ أَجَّةَ الظَلِيمِ [explained above: see 1].

أُجَاجٌ Anything burning to the mouth, whether salt or bitter or hot. (MF.) [Hence,] مَآءٌ أُجَاجٌ, (S, A, K, &c.,) and, (Msb,) Water that burns by its saltness: (A:) or salt water: or bitter water: (TA:) or salt, bitter water: (S, K:) or very salt water: (I' Ab:) or bitter and very salt water: (Msb:) or very salt water, that burns by reason of its saltness: or very bitter water: or water very salt and bitter, like the water of the sea: (TA:) or water of which no use is made for drinking, or…
أَجُوجٌ Giving light; shining; or shining brightly. (AA, S, K.)
أَجِيجٌ inf. n. of 1, which see: and see also أَجَّةٌ, in three places.
هَجِيرٌ أَجَّاجٌ [ A vehemently hot, or fiercelyburning, summer-midday ]. (A.)
أجُّ; fem. with ة: see الأَوَاججُ, below.
السَّمَائِمُ الأَوَاجِجُ [ The fiercely-burning hot winds; the latter word being pl. of, fem. of, which is the act. part. n. of أَجَّ;] is used by poetic licence for الأَوَاجُّ. (TA.)
ٱئسِتجَاجٌ inf. N. of 8, which see: and see also أَجَةٌ.

يَأْجُوجٌ One who walks quickly, and runs, in this and that manner. (K, * TA.) يَأْجُوجُ and, (S, Msb, K,) imperfectly decl., (S,) [ Gog and Magog; ] two tribes of God's creatures; (TA;) or two great nations; (Msb;) or two tribes of the children of Japheth the son of Noah: or, as some say, the former, of the Turks; and the latter, of the Jeel [meaning Jeel-Jeelán, said in the TA in art.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
